reason: The stems are fading, so I want to lift the potatoes into the basket for sorting and eating.
expectation: I expect a harvested batch of potatoes, though I don't know its condition yet.

alternatives.reason: Watering the trough is possible, but the chapter suggests the crop is ready to harvest.

effect: The harvest is available, and its size confirms the crop grew; I can sort seed stock before cooking.
reaction: The image of lifting pale potatoes larger than the seed pieces is a satisfying payoff.
reason: I want to set aside healthy potatoes for another planting, so the sorting bench seems the natural next place.
expectation: I expect the harvest to be sorted into seed stock and potatoes for eating, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Washing could prepare the harvest for eating, but I want to sort the seed first.

effect: The seed stock is selected and its goal is complete; I can now prepare potatoes to eat.
reaction: That was clear and practical, although I would have liked to know how healthy seed potatoes were selected.
reason: Washing the lifted potatoes is a natural preparation for cooking them.
expectation: I expect clean potatoes ready for cutting or cooking.

effect: The potatoes are washed, so cutting them is the next available food preparation.
reaction: A predictable and useful step, with nothing especially surprising.
reason: The knife should prepare the washed potatoes for cooking.
expectation: I expect cut potatoes, perhaps slices or pieces for the oven.

effect: The potatoes are cut and can now be dressed for cooking.
reaction: The result matches my expectation; the sequence is becoming routine.
reason: Oil on cut potatoes makes sense before roasting them in the galley oven.
expectation: I expect oiled potato pieces ready for the oven.

effect: The pieces are oiled and ready for the oven.
reaction: The preparation is straightforward, though each small action feels a little repetitive.
reason: Roasting the potatoes should fulfill the goal of tasting the harvest.
expectation: I expect cooked potatoes and perhaps a description of the meal.

effect: The potatoes are roasted and eaten, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The hot tray and quiet radio give the meal a lonely, grounded atmosphere; I liked that detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Lifting the potatoes was a satisfying payoff to the long wait, with the detail that they grew larger than the seed pieces.

leastWorthwhile.text: Washing, cutting and oiling were sensible but each separate action was predictable and became repetitive.

surprise.text: The quiet hiss of the radio during the meal added a lonely note I had not expected.

arbitrary.text: The actions I chose had clear purposes, but selecting healthy seed stock gave no detail on what made it healthy, which left the selection opaque.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see what happens to the discovery in the ice and the return journey; this chapter's quiet meal also made the expedition feel lived in, although the cooking sequence offered little challenge.
